descSub: 281 of the 500 come from a vocabulary
281 of the {n} come from a vocabulary
every form of a noun or a verb added together. The cards are dealt by that frequency, so the words you meet most often come first.

every form of a noun or a verb added together; and {added} more were added in November 2026 because a beginner needs them before either list would have dealt them: नमस्कार, zero, thirteen to nineteen and six of the tens, moved down from Hindi A2, seven everyday formulas moved from the phrases deck (आप कैसे हैं, मैं ठीक हूँ, आपका नाम क्या है, माफ़ कीजिए, जी हाँ, जी नहीं, कोई बात नहीं), and चाहिए and मेरा नाम … है, which no deck had. THE ORDER IS A TEACHING ORDER. The first {head} words are chosen by hand: the greetings and courtesies, a first exchange (how are you, I am fine, my name is), the pronouns and possessives, the commonest postpositions and verbs, the question words, zero to ten, and a dozen words every sentence leans on. After them the words come by that frequency, the commonest first, with three closed sets kept together: the days of the week from word {daysAt}, the colours from word {coloursAt} and the numbers above ten from word {numbersAt}. AT TEN NEW CARDS A DAY, the default for a language deck, both directions of a word arrive together, so this is five words a day: नमस्ते is the first card, the courtesies take {courtesyDays} days and the whole deck {days}.
behind the All forms fold their present, future, subjunctive and imperative by person.

behind the All forms fold their present, future, subjunctive and imperative by person; होना, to be, also shows है, था and होगा there. The possessives and का show the forms that agree (मेरा, मेरी, मेरे), an adjective that never changes is marked invariable, and a verb that is also used after another verb (रहना for the progressive, जाना for the passive) says so.

descSub: Within each subdeck the expressions come in the order of how many of Tatoeba's Hindi sentences contain them,

WHERE TO BEGIN: within each subdeck the expressions are grouped by the lowest level deck whose words and forms spell them — {a1} with Hindi A1 alone ({phrasesA1} of the {phrases} everyday phrases), then {a2}, {b1}, {b2} and {c1} that need A2, B1, B2 and C1, and last the {none} that use a word no level cards — so the everyday phrases can be begun beside Hindi A1, and the proverbs, none of which A1 alone spells, are better left until B1. At ten new cards a day, five expressions, the deck's {cards} cards take {days} days. Seven of the commonest formulas (आप कैसे हैं, माफ़ कीजिए, कोई बात नहीं …) are cards of Hindi A1 and not repeated here.
